# Landing page design references

Curated landing pages Elena keeps as design references. Each entry links to a subpage with live screenshots and captions.

Site: https://elenacabrera.xyz
Collections: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections?type=landing

## Superlogical
- URL: https://superlogical.com/
- Subpage: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/landings/superlogical/
- Tags: devtools, productivity, ai
- Design focus: Ultra-minimal devtool landing that sells a technical vision through long-form editorial copy and a single bold gradient visual anchor instead of product UI chrome.
- Screenshots:
  - Split hero with gradient: Left-aligned headline and layered keyword stack sit opposite a tall rounded gradient block, establishing a typographic-first hero with almost no chrome.
  - Three-step product vision: A manifesto section lays out a numbered three-part plan beside the same gradient motif, using restrained hierarchy and generous whitespace to sell a technical vision.
  - Founder pedigree grid: Team bios with headshots and heavyweight prior-company credentials create authority through pedigree rather than logos or metrics.
  - Investor list and waitlist: Named investor columns and a minimal underline-style email capture close the page, using social proof density plus a low-friction beta signup.

## Typo
- URL: https://www.typo.so/
- Subpage: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/landings/typo/
- Tags: productivity, ai
- Design focus: Soft, cloud-themed consumer SaaS landing that uses floating modular cards and bento layouts to show a flexible workspace product.
- Screenshots:
  - Username claim hero: A sky-background hero centers a username claim field while orbiting content cards preview integrations like Spotify and audio, selling modularity through scattered UI tiles.
  - Product canvas preview: A large rounded product mockup demonstrates the bento workspace layout with profile blocks, media widgets, and folder navigation under a concise value headline.
  - Persona icon columns: Four equal columns with 3D icons segment the audience into Creator, Builder, Artist, and Brand, using playful illustration to broaden appeal.
  - Orbital feature hub: A radial layout places the brand at the center with orbiting capability icons for AI, storage, shop, and blogging, visualizing an all-in-one platform.
  - Quote testimonial row: Minimal bordered cards in a horizontal row carry short user quotes with lots of negative space, keeping social proof light and airy.
  - Privacy and share features: A split grid pairs short feature copy with simple UI controls like a public/private toggle and circular share menu to explain publishing workflows.
  - Community closing CTA: A centered headline and pill button are ringed by user avatars, using circular social proof to reinforce a personal, community-driven product.

## EliseAI
- URL: https://eliseai.com/healthai
- Subpage: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/landings/eliseai/
- Tags: ai, health, enterprise
- Design focus: Enterprise healthcare AI landing that combines bold gradient heroes, compliance badges, and proof-heavy mid-page sections.
- Screenshots:
  - Healthcare demo hero: A blue gradient hero pairs a demo-booking form with HIPAA and G2 trust marks and a floating scheduling card mockup showing VoiceAI output.
  - Customer video carousel: A centered headline introduces a horizontal video testimonial carousel with client logos overlaid on thumbnails, prioritizing founder/operator proof.
  - VoiceAI product split: A dark split section contrasts copy and CTA on the left with a phone mockup on the right, then transitions into a white feature headline block below.
  - Specialty coverage grid: A 2x2 grid maps healthcare specialties to photo-backed cards with Learn More links, tailoring the product to vertical use cases.
  - Benefits and integrations: A dark three-column icon grid quantifies operational benefits before a white integrations section cites EHR compatibility and SOC 2/HIPAA compliance.
  - Competitive comparison table: A highlighted EliseAI column with checkmarks versus gray competitor columns uses a classic us-vs-them table to communicate feature superiority.
  - Resource links and FAQ: Three case-study link columns sit above a large FAQ accordion, handling late-funnel objections with expandable technical questions.

## Visitors
- URL: https://visitors.now/
- Subpage: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/landings/visitors/
- Tags: analytics
- Design focus: Polished indie-analytics SaaS page with floating nav, lavender gradients, and product-led hero previews.
- Screenshots:
  - Dashboard hero preview: A centered headline and dual CTAs sit above a logo strip and tabbed dashboard mockup embedded in a soft purple gradient, showing the product immediately.
  - Color-coded feature bento: A 2x2 card grid uses distinct accent colors and mini charts or globe visuals to explain revenue attribution, realtime tracking, profiles, and performance metrics.
  - Competitor comparison table: A highlighted Visitors column compares GDPR, revenue, and journey features against GA, Plausible, and Fathom in a clean matrix layout.
  - Usage-based pricing: A split pricing card combines a monthly/yearly toggle, event slider, and included-features checklist with a simulated globe visualization on the right.
  - FAQ accordion: A minimalist accordion addresses privacy, limits, and Google Analytics comparisons, with one expanded answer explaining no-cookie compliance.

## Midday
- URL: https://midday.ai/
- Subpage: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/landings/midday/
- Tags: fintech, invoicing, productivity
- Design focus: Clean fintech/productivity landing with serif hero typography, step-based product walkthroughs, and structured case-study social proof.
- Screenshots:
  - Serif hero with acquisition badge: A centered serif headline and single black CTA sit beneath a pill announcement badge, with faint integration logos providing quiet credibility before a dark product preview band.
  - How it works stepper: A vertical step list on the left highlights the active workflow stage while a crisp transaction table mockup on the right demonstrates unified banking data.
  - Feature grid headline: A centered section title introduces the full product surface area— invoicing, transactions, time tracking— before a bento-style capability grid below.
  - Invoicing feature card: Large rounded cards pair short benefit copy with embedded invoice UI previews, using alternating layouts to walk through core finance workflows.
  - Accounting time-savings proof: A bold 4–6 hours savings callout anchors a section about accounting readiness, quantifying operational benefit with oversized numerals instead of testimonial quotes.
  - Built with users band: A community-forward section uses avatar stacks and short founder quotes to show the product is shaped alongside real operators, not shipped in isolation.
  - Footer navigation close: A multi-column footer with Features, Product, Company, and Resources links closes the page with information density and minimal visual noise.

## Arche

- Tags: ai, devtools, productivity

- Screenshots:

  - Retro problem cards: Three tall cards use grainy vintage photos and short pain-point labels like the glue and the silos before a bold mission statement about irreplaceable decisions.
  - One harness diagram: An alternating text-and-diagram section shows fragmented copy-paste between Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Notion flowing into a single Arche harness.
  - Integrations library grid: A dense 4-column connector grid lists major SaaS tools with one-line capability descriptions, signaling breadth through recognizable logos and uniform cards.
  - Open-source mission: A centered manifesto section with a highlighted needs to exist headline and three bordered principle cards explains why the project is public and self-hostable.
  - FAQ accordion: A warm-background FAQ uses serif heading typography and simple plus icons in a spacious vertical list aimed at differentiation from ChatGPT and Notion.
  - Final action CTA: A gradient footer block pairs a pixel-styled Death to busywork headline with See it in action and Self-host now buttons for dual conversion paths.

## Ramp

- Design focus: Enterprise fintech landing with lime accent CTAs, live product UI in the hero, and data-visualization sections that turn complex finance workflows into scannable proof.
- Screenshots:

  - Efficiency comparison chart: A stippled bar chart card visualizes cost-per-token differences between efficient and inefficient teams beside explanatory copy and a See how you compare link.
  - Savings stats and testimonials: Oversized percentage stats in dark cards lead into a three-column testimonial row from finance leaders, mixing quantitative proof with operator quotes.
  - Weekly briefing feature: An alternating layout places a briefing UI mockup opposite copy about translating tokens into explainable dollars, showing product depth through realistic dashboard chrome.
  - Ramp Router API: A minimal gray product card with task prompts and a loading indicator supports a concise API value prop about cutting inference costs through one endpoint.
  - FAQ and closing CTA: A ruled FAQ accordion addresses AI spend objections before a repeated email-capture CTA closes the page with the core Time is money headline.
  - Logo strip social proof: A horizontal logo marquee of ambitious companies reinforces scale claims above late-page feature sections, using grayscale marks for understated credibility.

  - AI stack feature bento: Your entire AI stack in one place grids memory folders, branded visual outputs, meeting transcription chips, and If/Then automation cards — product capability without a bullet dump.
  - Chatbots versus Strawberry: A two-column compare stacks cluttered chatbot windows with red X marks against a single Strawberry tab with a labelled companion cursor and green checks for in-tab research and team collaboration.
  - Testimonial card grid: Loved by ambitious teams packs a 3x2 quote grid with headshots from Zapier, Float, and others, keeping social proof typographic and card-quiet before the security band.
  - Chat-style FAQ: A FAQ presented as stacked message bubbles — white questions, one black answer — sits beside Contact Us / See how it works CTAs and a blue companion reading a book.

# Launch videos

Curated product launch films Elena keeps as motion and narrative references. Each entry links to a subpage with an embedded video, timeline, design highlights, and palette.

Site: https://elenacabrera.xyz
Collections: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections?type=launch-video

## Mila (Capchase)
- Source: https://x.com/GuliMoreno/status/2110370319638954119
- Product: https://www.capchase.com/
- Subpage: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/mila-capchase/
- Company: Capchase
- Date: 2026-10-14
- Duration: 0:53
- Voiceover: no
- Tags: ai, fintech, motion
- Description: 53-second, no-voiceover motion-graphics launch for Capchase's AI deal-desk agent Mila: inbox chaos, Meet Mila on the bass drop, a frosted proposal demo, then scale and a finance.new end card. Made by Guli Moreno with Claude Code + HyperFrames; track Terminal Velocity by Cospe (Epidemic Sound).
- Timeline:
  - 0:00-0:03 Problem: Typed 'Traditional vendor financing is broken.' on a blank field; 'is broken.' goes bold on a tense typing beat.
  - 0:03-0:11 Overwhelm: Vertical waterfall of financing emails motion-blurs; three late-night chat bubbles and a notification pile on as the music builds.
  - 0:11-0:14 Pivot: Screen clears; 'But it doesn't have to be that way.' types, then a lavender highlight block; riser into silence.
  - 0:14-0:17 Meet Mila: Drop: concentric rings, fluid orange/peach orb, 'Meet Mila.'
  - 0:17-0:30 Demo: Orb docks into 'Ask Mila anything'; quote → credit check → proposal card → upfront tweak → Send → Pay now → Signed, on a macro zoom of the orb gradient.
  - 0:30-0:35 Channels: Quick cuts: 'Just ask.' then Via Gmail / Slack / finance.new in a light theme with real product UI.
  - 0:35-0:40 Callback: Same frantic bubbles return; Mila answers instantly with approvals and send confirmations.
  - 0:40-0:45 Scale: Camera pulls back to an infinite isometric card grid: 'A 24/7 deal desk.' / 'With instant answers.'
  - 0:45-0:53 CTA: Orange circular wipe to Capchase lockup, tagline 'Vendor financing at the speed of sales.', cursor clicks finance.new.
- Highlights:
  - 0:02 Typing as rhythm: Keystrokes land on the tense beat so the problem line feels scored, not just typed.
  - 0:08 Motion blur for overwhelm: Email rows streak vertically; speed itself becomes the metaphor for a broken desk.
  - 0:14 Highlight block as gear-shift: Lavender selection on the pivot line telegraphs the cut into silence before the drop.
  - 0:16 Orb as character: The orange/peach orb is logo, loader and avatar in one object that carries the Meet Mila hit.
  - 0:24 Macro-gradient backgrounds: Demo cards sit on a zoomed slice of the same orb gradient, so UI and brand stay one surface.
  - 0:37 Callback resolves the problem: The same late-night pings return with instant Mila replies — problem shot paid off, not abandoned.
  - 0:42 Isometric infinite grid: One card becomes a plane of deal-desk tiles; scale without a number counter.
- Narrative: Problem, pivot, Meet Mila on the drop, step-by-step demo, channels, callback that answers the opening chaos, scale, then end card. No voiceover — on-screen type and the Epidemic track carry the arc.
- Palette: #F5F6F8 (bg), #111111 (text), #E85D36 (Mila / emphasis), #F69D79 (peach), #D2C4ED (lavender pivot), #FFFFFF (cards)
- How it was made:
  - Tools: Claude Code; HyperFrames (HTML + GSAP → MP4); Epidemic Sound (Terminal Velocity by Cospe); ffmpeg / contact sheets / librosa / whisper for reference analysis
  - Article: https://www.gulipad.com/writings/mila-launch-video
  - Tip — Start with references, not the brief: Rank and study launch films before product context, music, or script. Shared references beat a cold brief.
  - Tip — Music first, drop on 'Meet Mila': Pick the track before visuals and lock cuts to measured onsets. The bass drop lands on Meet Mila; the logo lands on the last hit.
  - Tip — Be blunt, but say what works: Reviews can be harsh ("teletienda", "AI slop") if they also name the beat that is already right and ask for more of it.
  - Tip — Commit what's good: Git commits are save points and a clear signal not to rewrite the parts that already work.
  - Tip — Course-correct on the go: Send mid-task nudges instead of waiting for a full pass to finish.
  - Tip — Ask for its opinion: When a half of the film stalls, ask what is missing and let the model propose the next move.
  - Tip — Keep the taste calls: Human picks SFX links, tagline, and message-carrying lines; the agent handles execution and measurement.
  - Craft: Reference music often hits hardest ~70% in after 1–2s of silence; Attio uses a sub swell, Raycast slams every cut, Rippling peaks on the product name and the logo.
  - Craft: Script rule: ~12 headline lines max, one idea per film, product carries the story, single CTA.
  - Craft: Camera never stalls: constant drift plus punch-ins (shared expo.out curve); more short overlapping scenes beat fewer long ones.
  - Craft: Transitions should morph what is already on screen (Attio approach), not hard-cut to new content.
  - Craft: Avoid AI-slop: number counters, glitches, crack effects, cheesy SFX.
  - Craft: Epidemic Creator plan excludes brand marketing — need Business/Enterprise and swap preview stems for licensed masters.
  - Article vs final: The article's in-chat cut (30 fps) differs from the final X post (60 fps) after ~20s: opening line is 'Traditional vendor financing is broken.' (not 'Software and hardware…'); the 'Just ask.' / Via channels section is light-theme with real Gmail and Slack UIs instead of dark glass; scale line is 'A 24/7 deal desk. With instant answers.'; end tagline is 'Vendor financing at the speed of sales.' not '…speed of tech.'
  - References studied:
    - Ask Attio (1 — Guli's top pick): https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/attio-ask-attio/
    - New Raycast — Coming 2026 (2): https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/raycast-coming-2026/
    - Reception by ElevenLabs (3): https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/elevenlabs-reception/
    - Claude Slides, Design & Docs (4): https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/claude-slides-design-docs/
    - Harvey II (5): https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/harvey-ii/
    - Rippling AI (Added later as a key structure reference (two peaks: product name + logo)): https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/rippling-ai/
    - Ramp Accounting Bench: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/ramp-accounting-bench/
    - Hebbia Projects: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/hebbia-projects/
    - Linear Agent: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/linear-agent/
    - Ramp Policy Agent (Weakest of the set; kept as fintech reference): https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/ramp-policy-agent/
    - Superhuman power tools: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/superhuman/
    - Cursor 2.0: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/cursor-2-0/
    - Notion 3.0 Agents: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/notion-3-0-agents/
    - Krea 2: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/krea-2/
    - Chatly × Flowjam: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/chatly-flowjam/

- Source: https://x.com/charles_maddock/status/2114659351470247986

- Company: Strawberry
- Date: 2026-10-26
- Duration: 1:30
- Voiceover: no
- Tags: ai, browser, productivity, motion
- Description: 90-second, no-voiceover launch film: 3D AI 'companion' characters, kinetic type and abstracted app UIs on a white dot grid, driven by an upbeat electronic track and UI sound effects.
- Landing: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/landings/strawberry/
- Found via: https://elenacabrera.xyz/collections/launch-videos/mila-capchase/
- Timeline:
  - 0:00-0:05 Hook: Kinetic type ('You have plans', 'You want to move fast', 'You need a team') with characters running; establishes the need for speed and scale.
  - 0:05-0:11 Solution: 'The AI team that works alongside you'; words take on the characters' colours, characters pop into a command bar.
  - 0:11-0:30 Demo, sales: 'Book 100 sales calls' leads to automated LinkedIn outreach and Google Calendar filling up, then what companions can do across apps.
  - 0:30-0:47 Demo, collaboration: Multiple coloured cursors build a Google Slides research deck in parallel.
  - 0:47-0:57 Demo, admin: Google Meet note-taking, then Gmail follow-up, HubSpot update and the next call booked.
  - 0:57-1:07 Demo, organisation: Cursors drag scattered Google Drive files into department folders.
  - 1:08-1:16 Proof: '1.8 billion websites', floating SaaS icons, cascading testimonial cards, a ticking companions counter (267k+).
  - 1:17-1:29 CTA: 'Discover a new way to work', character lineup, end card with logo, 'Download now for free', Mac/Windows buttons, URL.
- Highlights:
  - 0:01 Kinetic type with colour binding: Bold, tightly tracked sans; words swap in place and take on each character's colour, tying copy to the product.
  - 0:10 Functional palette: Neutral white/grey dot grid plus soft accents, roughly purple #8762D9, coral #EB6B56, green #94C973, blue #75A9D2, each tied to a 'department' or companion.
  - 0:18 Abstracted UI framing: Real apps (LinkedIn, Slides) shown as clean floating white cards with soft shadows and no browser chrome, so focus stays on the action.
  - 0:27 Snappy motion and easing: Fast-in, slow-out; elements pop and scale with slight overshoot and slide off quickly, which reads as speed.
  - 0:43 Oversized coloured cursors: Stylised cursors in the character palette make invisible AI actions tangible.
  - 0:46 Multi-agent visualisation: Several cursors building one deck at once, a visual metaphor for a team working in parallel.
  - 1:11 Layered social proof: Testimonial cards cascade and overlap, then a fast-ticking counter, so it reads as lots of praise without slowing the pace.
  - 1:24 High-contrast end card: Characters stripped away: white, black/coral type, OS download buttons, URL. Zero ambiguity.
- Narrative: A compressed Problem, Solution, Proof, Action arc built for social feeds. It hooks on a universal desire (move fast without the headcount), introduces the companions as the team, rapid-fires four tedious tasks being automated in familiar apps, overwhelms with scale and social proof, and lands on a frictionless free-download CTA.
- Palette: #FFFFFF (approximate), #8762D9 (approximate), #EB6B56 (approximate), #94C973 (approximate), #75A9D2 (approximate), #111111 (approximate)
